paper_metadata.title: The Effect of Age on Functional Outcome in Mild Traumatic Brain Injury: 6-Month Report of a Prospective Multicenter Trial

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: While the study describes the source population and inclusion criteria well, the enrollment rate was only 30%, and the final sample size for the elderly cohort was small (n=44), which may limit representativeness.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Adult patients (age > 18 years) admitted to one of the four trauma centers between January 2000 and July 2002 were eligible for enrollment if they sustained blunt TBI with head Abbreviated Injury Scale (AIS) score greater than 3 and an AIS score to any other body area of less than 1 and they survived to discharge.
items.reasoning: The authors clearly define the age, injury type (blunt TBI), and severity (AIS) of the target population.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: The study was conducted at four Level I trauma centers... Using data from trauma registries at the four centers, the enrollment rate for the study was approximately 30%.
items.reasoning: The use of four Level I trauma centers and trauma registries provides a clear sampling frame, though the low enrollment rate is noted.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: between January 2000 and July 2002
items.reasoning: The specific dates for recruitment are provided.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: New Jersey Trauma Center... University of California at San Diego... San Francisco General Medical Center... and Harborview Medical Center, University of Washington, Seattle, Washington.
items.reasoning: The specific hospitals and geographic locations are listed.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: eligible for enrollment if they sustained blunt TBI with head Abbreviated Injury Scale (AIS) score greater than 3 and an AIS score to any other body area of less than 1 and they survived to discharge. Patients who had minor facial or orbital fractures (AIS score of 2) that did not require operative fixation were also included... Patients with prolonged loss of consciousness without a definite injury on computed tomographic scanning were not included.
items.reasoning: Detailed AIS-based inclusion and exclusion criteria are provided.

items.label: Adequate study participation
items.prompt: There is adequate participation in the study by eligible individuals
items.evidence_snippet: the enrollment rate for the study was approximately 30%. Reasons for nonenrollment included patient under custody, translator not available, and patient discharged before being approached for consent.
items.reasoning: A 30% enrollment rate is low, raising concerns about whether the participants differ systematically from those not enrolled, though the authors claim no demographic differences.

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Forty-nine percent of the study population were white, 22% Hispanic, 18% black, and 10% Asian. A higher percentage of the elderly were women (46%) than the young adults (19%) (p=0.003). Mechanism of injury was most likely to be fall in the elderly group... Mean GCS score of the entire population was 12.8
items.reasoning: Race, gender, mechanism of injury, and GCS are reported for the baseline sample.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The 6-month follow-up rate was 70% (28% lost to follow-up), which is below the ideal 80% threshold. While the authors state it is unlikely to cause selective bias, the characteristics of those lost were not fully compared to those who completed.

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis
items.prompt: Response rate (i.e., proportion of study sample completing the study and providing outcome data) is adequate.
items.evidence_snippet: One hundred twenty-eight patients (70%) in the mild TBI group were evaluable at 6 months for follow-up (2 patients had died and 52 (28%) were lost to follow-up).
items.reasoning: 70% follow-up is acceptable but not ideal for limiting attrition bias.

items.label: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out
items.prompt: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out of the study are described.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: The text does not describe specific efforts made to contact or retrieve data for those lost to follow-up.

items.label: Reasons and potential impact of subjects lost to follow-up
items.prompt: Reasons for loss to follow-up are provided.
items.evidence_snippet: 52 (28%) were lost to follow-up
items.reasoning: The text states they were lost but does not provide specific reasons (e.g., moved, refused, unable to contact).

items.label: Outcome and prognostic factor information on those lost to follow-up
items.prompt: Participants lost to follow-up are adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: There is no table or description comparing the characteristics of those lost to follow-up versus those who remained.

items.prompt: There are no important differences between key characteristics (LIST) and outcomes in participants who completed the study and those who did not.
items.evidence_snippet: The follow-up rate for this study, both for the elderly and for the young, suggests that it is unlikely that selective loss to follow-up of lower functioning adults accounts for the overall good functional outcome.
items.reasoning: The authors assume no bias, but provide no data to support the claim that those lost were similar to those who stayed.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Study Attrition Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Loss to follow-up (from baseline sample to study population analyzed) is not associated with key characteristics (i.e., the study data adequately represent the sample) sufficient to limit potential bias to the observed relationship between PF and outcome.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The primary prognostic factor (age) is an objective demographic variable, and the study used a clear cut-off (65 years) while also acknowledging the continuous nature of age.

items.reasoning: Age is clearly defined and categorized.

items.evidence_snippet: we divided the elderly group at age 65 based on our prior work in an increased mortality after TBI.
items.reasoning: The cut-point was based on prior literature/work, not data-driven from the current sample.

risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: PF is adequately measured in study participants to sufficiently limit potential bias.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: Primary outcome assessed was functional outcome at discharge and 6 months postdischarge as measured by both Glasgow Outcome Scale (GOS) score and a modified FIM score
items.reasoning: Outcomes and follow-up timing are explicitly defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: The use of subgroups from the FIM has been demonstrated to track changes in functional status as well as the total FIM... All individuals assigning the patients GOS and FIM scores underwent instruction by the principal investigator at each site
items.reasoning: The authors cite validity studies for the modified FIM and describe standardized training for raters.

items.reasoning: Standardized personnel and tools were used across all participants.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study controlled for extracranial injuries by using an 'isolated TBI' design and performed subgroup analysis by GCS. However, it did not use multivariable regression to adjust for other potential confounders like pre-existing comorbidities or specific neurosurgical interventions.

items.evidence_snippet: Data collected included demographics, GCS score at admission, and neurosurgical interventions... 73% (n=32) had preinjury medical conditions
items.reasoning: Key confounders like GCS and interventions were measured, but detailed comorbidities were only partially captured.

items.evidence_snippet: GCS score at admission... neurosurgical intervention (craniotomy, placement of an intracranial pressure monitor, and use of medications to control cerebral perfusion pressure)
items.reasoning: Confounders like GCS and specific interventions are well-defined.
